title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention with timeouts
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: The continuous-batcher scheduler has shown periodic unfairness where long-running high-token requests can starve small, latency-sensitive requests in high-concurrency workloads. This PR tunes queueing behavior, introduces per-priority starvation prevention, and adds configurable timeouts to reduce queue head-of-line blocking. Key changes: 1) Implement a priority-aware queueing layer that tracks per-priority waiting time and enforces a fairness promotion when a request exceeds a configurable starvation threshold. 2) Add soft timeouts at the queue level that trigger a lower-cost fallback path (quantized model or reduced max tokens) when the scheduler cannot meet the latency SLO for latency-sensitive priorities. 3) Improve scheduler accounting to prefer small requests in mixed workloads by estimating expected token-processing time using model kernel profiles and request length histograms. 4) Expose new config flags (batcher.queue.starvation_threshold_ms, batcher.queue.promotion_chance, batcher.queue.soft_timeout_ms, batcher.queue.fallback_profile) and wire them into the default runtime config with conservative defaults. 5) Add unit and integration tests that simulate mixed workloads and verify fairness metrics (95th token-serve latency per-priority) do not regress. 6) Add telemetry: new metrics batcher_queue_wait_ms_by_priority, batcher_starvation_promotions, batcher_soft_timeout_triggers; and associated dashboard snippets. Backwards compatibility: Flags default to off/large values so behavior is unchanged unless tuned. Rollout plan: feature flag gated for 2 weeks in canary, nightly performance runs, then full rollout. See linked Linear ENG-4123 for perf target and ENG-4189 for rollout steps. Testing: local unit tests, perf-canary runs on small cluster, and a synthetic mixed-workload suite that reproduced the original starvation symptom. Notes: tuned constants chosen to avoid oscillation under load; further tuning may be needed for specific customer profiles.

review_comments: Marco Silva: The promotion logic looks reasonable, but can we avoid promoting too aggressively under bursty load? Suggest adding a probabilistic promotion cap or backoff.
Priya Natarajan: Addressed - added promotion_chance config and backoff window to limit repeated promotions for the same priority bucket.
Jasmine Patel: CI flake on first run (integration timeout). Re-ran and all checks passed. Can you add a small test validating fallback_profile selection when soft timeout triggers?
Priya Natarajan: Added fallback selection unit test and an integration scenario in mixed_workload.rs that asserts fallback is taken when soft timeout elapsed.
Liam O'Connor: Suggest adding a metric to count requests demoted to fallback so SRE can alert on excessive fallback usage.
Priya Natarajan: Added batcher_soft_timeout_triggers metric and increment hook where fallback is applied. Updated dashboard snippets in docs.
ci_checks: bench/perf-canary: queued for nightly; preliminary local perf shows 8-12% reduction in 95th latency for small requests in mixed workload
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler fairness: new per-priority starvation prevention, queue-level soft timeouts with fallback profile, and telemetry. Config flags added under batcher.queue.* with conservative defaults. No behavioral changes unless flags are tuned.
